newsitem.title: UK: NWE diesel premiums firm, Asia arb starts to wane.
newsitem.headline: NWE diesel premiums firm, Asia arb starts to wane.

text.p: Resilient demand lifted European diesel cargo premiums slightly on Tuesday while arbitrage to the east narrowed on waning values in Asian markets, traders said.
Cargoes of low sulphur diesel moved basis Le Havre at a premium of $14 to April IPE gas oil futures for delivery before April 20, over one dollar firmer.
Another cargo changed hands at a $10.75 premium to April for delivery in the last decade of the month, again basis Le Havre.
Traders saw little interest for Russian material since most of the large 60,000 tonne vessels workable from Ventspils are in use for Asian trips.

On the barge market, a prompt parcel of 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil changed hands at a 25 cent premium to the April IPE, around unchanged. A barge for delivery in the second half of April changed hands at a 50 cent premium to April.
Spot barge traffic remains very quiet, depressed by demand running at well under the levels for the first quarter of 1997 that were being forecast several months ago.
Traders continue to try to move out intermediate grade low sulphur diesel to make way for summer grade but a standoff over values has slowed the offtake this week.
